title: Pakistan Foreign Office Rejects India's Terror-Network Allegations, Accuses India of 'State-Sponsored Terrorism' Abroad
detail: Pakistan's Foreign Office spokesperson Tahir Andrabi on August 18, 2026 rejected as 'baseless assertions' Home Minister Amit Shah's claim that the Shahzad Bhatti Network was Pakistan-backed, calling it part of a 'malicious campaign' to divert attention from India's domestic security challenges. Andrabi countered that 'unfounded Indian insinuations cannot divert international attention away from India's state-sponsored terrorism, targeted assassinations, and subversion in foreign territories,' citing convicted Indian naval officer Kulbhushan Jadhav as 'undeniable proof' of Indian involvement in subversion inside Pakistan, alongside Canadian and US allegations of Indian agents' involvement in plots against Sikh separatist activists. Pakistan urged the international community to hold India accountable for what it called state-sponsored terrorism in the region.

media.caption: Pakistan's Foreign Office rejects India's allegations linking it to the Shahzad Bhatti Network, accuses India of state-sponsored terrorism abroad, August 18, 2026
